subject: Computer Networking
title: Network Function Virtualization
description: A micro-lesson that makes Network Function Virtualization usable.

hook.text: Firewalls, load balancers, routers — each was a hardware box. NFV runs them all as software.

buildup.text: NFV replaces hardware appliances with VMs or containers. Same network functions, standard servers.

discovery.text: Telecoms pioneered NFV. Instead of racking a physical firewall, deploy a virtual one in minutes.

twist.text: NFV and SDN complement each other. SDN controls traffic flow; NFV provides the processing services.

climax.text: 5G relies on NFV. Core functions run as containers in data centers, not on proprietary hardware.

punchline.text: NFV moves network functions from hardware to software. Faster and cheaper.

quiz.question: What does NFV replace?
options: Dedicated hardware appliances with software running on standard servers

details.summary: Network function virtualization replaces dedicated hardware appliances like firewalls, routers, and load balancers with software running on standard servers.
details.whyItMatters: NFV eliminates the need to purchase and install proprietary hardware for every network function. It brings cloud-like agility to network services that previously required expensive specialized equipment.
takeaways: NFV runs network functions as software on commodity servers
Service chaining connects multiple virtual functions in sequence
Telcos use NFV to deploy services in minutes instead of months

faq.question: What network functions can be virtualized?
faq.answer: Almost any network function can be virtualized: firewalls, load balancers, WAN optimizers, intrusion detection systems, routers, and DNS servers. Telcos virtualize mobile network core functions.

faq.question: How does NFV relate to SDN?
faq.answer: SDN controls how traffic flows through the network. NFV virtualizes the functions that process that traffic. Together, SDN steers traffic to the right virtual network functions, which NFV runs on standard hardware. They are complementary approaches that work best in combination.
